messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Smart routing policy triggered cross-region fallback that routed traffic for a EU-data-residency customer to eu-west-1. Possible data residency violation. Auto-page sent to #incidents and oncall.
PagerDuty: Paging Mia Chen (oncall) and Samir Patel (backup).
Mia Chen: On it. Acknowledging. Which customers are affected?
Samir Patel: I'm seeing a chain: capacity shortage in us-east-1 -> routing policy allows region fallback -> fallback picks eu-west-1 because it's tagged compatible -> model variant selected is v1-quant (unverified encryption) -> some requests loop between routing layers when policy re-evaluates. Logging shows repeated route change for same request ids.
Mia Chen: Ok, priority is stop further cross-region routes to EU for customers with residency constraints. Can we flip the fallback policy to local-only?
Rajeev Kumar: I can apply an emergency gate. Patch available: disable cross-region fallback for tenant group "EU_RESIDENCY". Commit id: a3f9d2b. CLI to apply: 
```
redwoodctl routing-policy set --policy-id routing-xyz --no-cross-region-fallback --match tenant:EU_RESIDENCY
redwoodctl rollout set --target routing-xyz --mode immediate
```
Applying now.
Oncall Bot: Mia Chen set as incident lead; Samir Patel as secondary.
Mia Chen: Apply patch and verify. Also need to pin affected tenants to us-east-1 while we investigate model variant selection.
Samir Patel: Patch applied at 1768504360. Quick grep of logs shows misroutes starting at 1768504205. Sample log snippet: 
```
[1768504210] req=0x7f3a route_attempt=1 region=us-east-1 -> capacity=full
[1768504211] req=0x7f3a route_attempt=2 selected_region=eu-west-1 policy_reason=fallback_tag_match
[1768504212] req=0x7f3a model=v1-quant variant=encryption=none
[1768504213] req=0x7f3a route_recheck=1 selected_region=us-east-1 // loop
```
Rajeev Kumar: That loop is caused by our policy re-evaluation heuristic; it retries to preferred region but fallback policies are too permissive. I'll throttle re-eval to avoid flapping.
Elena Torres: I'll start the customer notification template for affected EU-residency customers. Which tenants? Samir?
Samir Patel: Affected tenants: tenant-eu-143, tenant-eu-198, tenant-eu-205. Sending list to compliance.
Elena Torres: Notifying legal/compliance now. Draft message: "We detected a transient routing event that may have routed data outside your region. We have implemented mitigations and will follow up with timeline and audit logs."
Incident Bot: Status update - cross-region fallback disabled for EU_RESIDENCY at 1768504360. Monitoring for further misroutes.
Mia Chen: Confirming no new misroutes for requests since 1768504380. Samir, can you confirm model variant restrictions?
Samir Patel: We've added an explicit allowlist for model variants per-region and pinned the tenants above to model v1-standard (approved). Command run: 
```
redwoodctl model-policy update --region us-east-1 --allowlist v1-standard --tenant tenant-eu-143,tenant-eu-198,tenant-eu-205
```
Change applied 1768504445.
Rajeev Kumar: Also reverted the recent routing-policy change from PR #482 (author: infra-ops) that introduced permissive fallback tags. Revert commit: b4c2e1f, rolled back at 1768504520.
Mia Chen: Good. Please lock the routing policy and open a change request for a proper canary test before re-enabling cross-region fallback.
Samir Patel: Running a quick enforcement scan for other tenants with residency labels — found 2 more potential mismatches, will flag in CR.
Elena Torres: Compliance ack: legal will need the full audit log for tenant-eu-143 and tenant-eu-205. I'll attach logs and timeline.
PagerDuty: Reminder: incident is P1. Next escalation in 10m if no resolution confirmed.
Samir Patel: Observability shows rate of misroutes dropped to 0 after 1768504380. I'm keeping an eye on routing traces.
Mia Chen: Handoff - I need to go to a pager quiet period in 15m. Samir, please take incident lead for the next 45m. Rajeev, please own the CR and postmortem. Elena, coordinate customer comms and compliance artifacts.
Oncall Bot: Handoff recorded. New lead: Samir Patel.
Samir Patel: Accepted lead. Will keep this as active until we close and verify audit export.
Incident Bot: Change applied: routing-policy locked (no more hot edits) at 1768504600.
Rajeev Kumar: Created CR-789 for safer fallback gating, will include canary, telemetry alerts for model-variant selection, and a test harness to prevent loop conditions. Assigned to infra-ops, ETA 72h.
Elena Torres: Customer notifications sent for tenant-eu-143 and tenant-eu-205 at 1768504800. Compliance acknowledged receipt.
Mia Chen: Quick status: Impacted requests total ~1.2k during the window, no evidence of persisted data transfer outside audits show ephemeral routing only but compliance to verify.
Samir Patel: Running final verification: replayed traces for sampled requests; encryption headers present in all us-east-1 deliveries, missing in eu-west-1 deliveries for ~3% of requests — those match model variant v1-quant. Those have been blocked.
Mia Chen: Great. Plan: keep cross-region fallback disabled for EU_RESIDENCY until CR complete, patch model-variant allowlist into policy, add unit/e2e tests for residency constraints.
Incident Bot: Incident status: mitigated. Monitoring continues. Please file postmortem with timeline and RCA.
Samir Patel: I'll run a final audit export and drop artifacts in the incident folder. Handoff: I'm primary for next 45m but Mia will return for postmortem.
Mia Chen: Thanks team. Closing on-call now.
Elena Torres: Filing customer follow-up tickets and compliance packet.
Rajeev Kumar: Postmortem placeholder created: /incidents/postmortems/1768504321-routing-residency-fallback-loop.md
Incident Bot: Incident marked resolved at 1768506120.
Mia Chen: Acknowledged. Will review postmortem and approve RCA. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
